newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo still talking on trucks with Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: Volvo still talking on trucks with Mitsubishi.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo on Monday said talks with Mitsubishi Corp of Japan over cooperation on truck operations in Europe and Asia will continue in 1997.
The two companies, which already produce cars at Dutch joint venture NedCar, agreed last week to strengthen their business ties and are in negotiations.
"We will do a pre-study and then we will make a decision," Volvo spokesman Stefan Lorentzon told Reuters.
"We are looking at all possibilites and that goes for production, product development and distribution."
A Mitsubishi spokesman last week said the two companies would consider selling commercial vehicles jointly in Europe and sharing car components globally and develop a new engine.
Volvo could perhaps use Mitsubishi's sales network in Asia.
But Lorentzon said nothing was yet settled.
"We are interested in going deeper into Asia and Mitsubishi wants to do the same in Europe," he said.
The companies said the agreement aimed to strengthen their competitiveness.
The NedCar plant, which began operations in 1989, is owned in three equal parts by the carmakers and the Dutch government.
It produces the medium-sized Volvo S40/V40 range and the Mitsubishi Carisma model.
Mitsubishi in October said it would supply its newly developed fuel-efficient gasoline injection engines (GDI) in the future for Volvo cars made at the NedCar plant.
